entries.test: Controlled training studies could establish whether training on substantial amounts of model-generated content provides useful learning or instead degrades performance.
entries.note: The claim makes a testable assertion about training effects despite its language about meaning and guesswork.
'I'd bet money' expresses a confident conjecture about the training corpus rather than an unqualified factual assertion.
The central claim recommends a strategy as OpenAI's best hope for survival.

entries.test: Controlled evaluations could show whether visual errors decrease without substantially more training data, while public dataset inventories could compare available visual and textual data.
entries.note: The word 'only' asserts a necessary condition that alternative successful methods could disprove.

entries.test: Public training studies and dataset inventories could establish whether limited synthetic-data methods resolve the asserted training-data shortage and how commonly generated data is used to address it.
entries.note: 'Broken tool' is rhetorical coloring around an empirical claim about data supply and proposed remedies.
The proposed explanation for the article's vagueness is explicitly qualified by 'likely.'

entries.test: Published investment agreements, contractual spending commitments, or financial disclosures could establish the claimed annual revenue guarantees and required cloud usage.
entries.note: Zitron asserts the contractual facts in his own voice while crediting a source. Currently private contracts do not make the facts inherently uncheckable.
'Isn't exactly exciting' is the central evaluative conclusion. The embedded revenue-disclosure and percentage assertions are separately checkable.

entries.test: Global equity-index returns for the first quarters of 2020–2024 and contemporaneous return-attribution evidence could establish the five-year comparison and AI's contribution.
entries.note: The market-performance assertion is firm and checkable. The accompanying fear about unstable hype is not independently settled by that test.

entries.test: Contemporaneous company financial results, data-center investment announcements, and cloud-provider earnings statements could establish who benefited financially and whether every major provider reported little AI revenue while expanding capacity.
entries.note: The surrounding financial discussion gives 'benefitting' a plain financial reading. 'Yet to prove its necessity' adds an evaluative qualification.

entries.test: Adoption surveys and documented production deployments available by April 2024 could establish whether evidence of actual AI adoption was limited.
entries.note: In context this assesses the available adoption evidence, rather than making a claim solely about his private awareness.

entries.test: Controlled hallucination evaluations could determine whether reductions require increased compute, while documented business failures and data-supply studies could assess the asserted harms.
entries.note: The exclusive claim about compute is falsifiable by effective methods that do not increase it. The dwindling resource in context is data.

entries.test: Historical financial evidence from recognized bubbles and contemporaneous reporting on OpenAI and Anthropic could establish the claimed financial pattern and whether revenue stories neglected profits.
entries.note: 'Never seem to' qualifies the characterization of coverage. A hallmark is an asserted recurring indicator, not proof that every loss-making industry is a bubble.

entries.test: Sustained commercially viable deployment of Sora or comparable generative-video products, or their abandonment because of the asserted resource and legal barriers, could settle the predicted commercial failure.
entries.note: In context 'dead on arrival' predicts commercial nonviability. No deadline is supplied.

entries.test: If core business adoption fails and the market turns, public revenue reports and layoff announcements could establish whether resulting efficiency cuts eliminate tens of thousands of jobs.
entries.note: The adoption failure and market reversal are stated conditions, not unconditional predictions.

entries.test: If AI fails to generate meaningful customer and provider profits, Nvidia's reported chip orders and sales could establish whether demand slows dramatically.
entries.note: 'Likely' qualifies Nvidia's early-warning role. The separate conditional prediction about chip orders is firm.
'I expect' is firm expectation, despite the drafter's 'likely' label. 'Far worse things' supplies no shared comparison across stock losses, operating losses, layoffs, or business failure.

entries.test: Public engineering studies, power-capacity records, and documented cooling constraints could establish whether heat and electricity were materially limiting further AI scaling at publication.
entries.note: The physical-constraint assertion is checkable in the article's scaling context. 'Mediocre' is a separate value judgment.
